subject: Negative Probability Given to Rank Sample

messages.author: 6d020fc5d7c9ee0a
messages.subject: Negative Probability Given to Rank Sample
parts:
Dear Nimble Users,

I am running into some issues using the Liu West Filter, which perhaps is due to how I'm specifying my model.  I'm not 100% sure.  Perhaps there is an initialization step I need to run first?   

When I run the Filter I am getting back "Negative Probability Given to Rank Sample." Below is the code I am running (with simulated data).   Any information or tips would be much appreciated.

Thanks,

Colin


library(nimble)

## Simulate Data#
set.seed(10)
t<-1:(365)
v<-rnorm(365,sd=0.5)
seasonal<-sin(2*pi*t/365) + cos(pi*2*t/365)
y<- seasonal + v
plot(y,type="p")



#Create Constant W, G and F matrices to pass to NIMBLE
W<-diag(2)
F<-matrix(c(1,0), nrow = 1, ncol = 2)
#G matrix; can generalize this later
G<-matrix(c(cos(2*pi/365),-sin(2*pi/365),sin(2*pi/365),cos(2*pi/365)),nrow=2,ncol=2)

smosCode <- nimbleCode({
  #Initial Values for State: x0 ~ Normal(c(0,0),diag(1000))
  m0[1]<-0
  m0[2]<-0
  C0[1:2,1:2]<-1000*W[1:2,1:2]
  x0[1:2]~dmnorm(m0[1:2],C0[1:2,1:2])
  
  #initial values
  m1[1:2,1]<-G[1:2,1:2]%*%x0[1:2]
  C1[1:2,1:2]<-sigmaSquaredInvw*W[1:2,1:2]
  x[1:2,1]~dmnorm(m1[1:2,1],C1[1:2,1:2])
  y[1]~dnorm(inprod(F[1,1:2],x[1:2,1]),sigmaSquaredInvv)
  
  #Model
  for (t in 2:T){
    mu[1:2,t]<-G[1:2,1:2]%*%x[1:2,t-1]
    sigs[1:2,1:2]<-sigmaSquaredInvw*W[1:2,1:2]
    x[1:2,t] ~ dmnorm(mu[1:2,t],sigs[1:2,1:2])
    y[t] ~ dnorm(inprod(F[1,1:2],x[1:2,t]),sigmaSquaredInvv)
  }
  
  #Priors 
  sigmaSquaredInvv~dgamma(5,20)
  sigmaSquaredInvw~dgamma(5,20)
})


smosModel<-nimbleModel(code=smosCode,constants=list(T=365,pi=pi,G=G,W=W,F=F),data=list(y=y),
                       inits=list(sigmaSquaredInvv=1,sigmaSquaredInvw=1))



smosLiuWestFilter<-buildLiuWestFilter(model=smosModel,nodes='x',params=c('sigmaSquaredInvv','sigmaSquaredInvw'))
csmosLiuWestFilter <- compileNimble(smosModel, smosLiuWestFilter)
csmosLiuWestFilter[[2]]$run(10000)

messages.subject: Re: Negative Probability Given to Rank Sample
parts:
Colin, thanks for your interest in NIMBLE, and great that you're using the new suite of SMC algorithms.

I'm not an expert with these, but I did take a look into your error.  I believe (hopefully) that it just boils down to incorrect parameterization of the multivariate normal distributions (dmnorm).  The default parameterization for the dmnorm() distribution takes the second parameter as a *precision* matrix, so as your model is written, the prior on x0 (for example) has precison=1000, and variance=1/1000 for each element.  I suspect you meant for these to be covariance matrices for each dmnorm term, and the small variances you were using were leading to numerical problems when propagating the particles.

Changing each dmnorm(...) to instead specify a covariance matrix (by naming the second parameter cov=...) cleans up the problem, and the algorithm runs fine -- and I believe gives realistic estimates for each variance term, if I'm following the algorithm correctly.

Anyway, give it a go.  I've copied the (very simply) modified model code below.  Good luck!

Daniel


smosCode <- nimbleCode({
    ##Initial Values for State: x0 ~ Normal(c(0,0),diag(1000))

m0[1]<-0
    m0[2]<-0
    C0[1:2,1:2]<-1000*W[1:2,1:2]

##x0[1:2]~dmnorm(m0[1:2],C0[1:2,1:2])
    x0[1:2]~dmnorm(m0[1:2],cov=C0[1:2,1:2])              ## using covariance
    ##initial values

m1[1:2,1]<-G[1:2,1:2]%*%x0[1:2]
    C1[1:2,1:2]<-sigmaSquaredInvw*W[1:2,1:2]

##x[1:2,1]~dmnorm(m1[1:2,1],C1[1:2,1:2])
    x[1:2,1]~dmnorm(m1[1:2,1],cov=C1[1:2,1:2])           ## using covariance
y[1]~dnorm(inprod(F[1,1:2],x[1:2,1]),sigmaSquaredInvv)
##Model

for (t in 2:T){
        mu[1:2,t]<-G[1:2,1:2]%*%x[1:2,t-1]
        sigs[1:2,1:2]<-sigmaSquaredInvw*W[1:2,1:2]

##x[1:2,t] ~ dmnorm(mu[1:2,t],sigs[1:2,1:2])
        x[1:2,t] ~ dmnorm(mu[1:2,t],cov=sigs[1:2,1:2])   ## using covariance

y[t] ~ dnorm(inprod(F[1,1:2],x[1:2,t]),sigmaSquaredInvv)
    }

##Priors 
    sigmaSquaredInvv~dgamma(5,20)
    sigmaSquaredInvw~dgamma(5,20)
})

Thanks, Daniel!  I think you are right.  I actually want everything in terms of precision, because of conjugacy with the gamma priors on the variance terms.  I will switch that first one over to precision and give it a go.

Cheers,

Colin
